A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AEIC research work. All 22 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures, references, and supplementary material, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression-quality experiments, computational measurements, ablations, and qualitative reconstructions on CLIC 2020, DIV2K, and Kodak.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results and adds a human preference study in Appendix C and Figure 11.

M1.justification: The AEIC architectures, entropy model, unconditional diffusion decoder, dual-side distillation, losses, and progressive training procedure are retained. Clarified descriptions and a corrected training-parameter symbol do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds a human-observer evaluation population through a 15-participant preference study on Kodak. The image datasets, compression task, and image-resolution coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their comparator sets. The new user study reuses H.266/VVC, DLF, and StableCodec, already compared in v1's Kodak qualitative evaluation. Naming PerCo as PerCo (SD) clarifies the community implementation already documented in v1.

E3.justification: The new user study introduces reference-assisted, side-by-side comparisons at similar ultra-low bitrates, randomized left-right placement, and 15 participants evaluating 24 cases each. Existing benchmark protocols remain unchanged; Table 5's new statement excluding HRF clarifies an existing experiment.

E4.justification: The new user preference analysis tests whether AEIC-SE's perceptual advantages are supported by human judgments. Existing analyses of compression ratio, distillation, high-resolution finetuning, encoder replacement, decoder pruning, and perceptual losses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new study reports aggregate preference percentages without uncertainty estimates; participant counts and randomized presentation concern its evaluation design.

E6.justification: New Figure 11 reports AEIC-SE preference rates of 96.2% against H.266/VVC, 82.7% against DLF, and 72.1% against StableCodec. AEIC-SE uses 0.0144 bpp versus 0.0145, 0.0156, and 0.0140 bpp, respectively. These are newly reported subjective results; existing tables, curves, and reconstruction examples are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 3.1.1 qualifies the O(M) = O(2^R) encoding-complexity argument: it now explicitly assumes exhaustive search without assumptions about codeword structure. This narrows a previously unqualified mathematical argument; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning shallow encoders, dual-side distillation, perceptual performance, and real-time 1080P encoding. The user study adds support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.1.1 refines the small-variance interpretation from restricting the value range to restricting likely sampled values. Section 4.3 extends the stated untiled 1080P feasibility from AEIC-SE to both AEIC variants, consistent with the retained Table 2. The decoding-latency limitation remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an AEIC code-access link, explicitly documents the exclusion of HRF in Table 5, and corrects the Stage 1 reset symbol from the student loss to lambda_S1. LoRA rank and distillation weights added to the main text were already disclosed in v1's appendix.

R1.justification: v2 adds CADC: Content Adaptive Diffusion-based Generative Image Compression to the diffusion-compression literature in Section 2.1. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata or ordering; the research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 locally condenses introductory and related-work prose, shortens the supplementary roadmap, adds a User Study section, and shifts subsequent appendix lettering. It also adds funding and corresponding-author information. The overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the user-preference bar chart as Figure 11, reflows nearby appendix content, and makes limited caption and table-formatting adjustments. Existing figures are retained, with subsequent appendix figures renumbered; printed page numbers are removed.

improvement.justification: The human preference study provides useful direct support for perceptual-quality claims previously supported by metrics and examples. The code-access link, clearer experimental disclosures, and qualified complexity argument also improve the paper. These gains are limited: the method and established results remain unchanged, and the small user study reports no uncertainty estimates.
